selection: mediabunny 1.66.0 (26,071,768 downloads) and codec-parser 2.5.0 (2,683,215) are two independent JavaScript MPEG frame-header parsers with documented local byte APIs (Input with BufferSource; CodecParser('audio/mpeg').parseAll(Uint8Array)), exact results on both untagged controls checked against the independent frame-header walker, V8 package source coverage and stable parser-derived AFL++ feedback. music-metadata (9,827,896) ranks between them with its own MPEG frame parser and remains an unbuilt lead; mpg123-decoder (2,505,430) wraps libmpg123.
uncertainty: Two verified paths; no padding. Search is six npm queries of 100 hits each, captured 2026-11-17; downloads were fetched for 15 hand-picked candidates, not every hit. mediabunny was found by `mp3 frame`, `mp3 duration` and `mp3 demuxer`, not the narrower queries. Download counts cover whole toolkits: mediabunny's muxing, conversion and many containers, and codec-parser's AAC, FLAC and Ogg parsers, not MP3 framing alone. music-metadata ranks above codec-parser and was not built here, so the two selected paths are not the top two by downloads. Neither path decodes Layer III audio. music-metadata and the mpg123 WASM wrappers are recorded as shared-family leads. Two untagged CBR controls do not establish VBR, Xing/Info, free-format, Layer I/II, MPEG-2.5, CRC-protected or ID3 support. No standard Node.js MP3 API exists. codec-parser's valid-control AFL++ differential is narrow: one header-cache range that tracks distinct frame headers, not version or channel branches. Its V8 line counts include module evaluation of imported AAC, FLAC, Opus, Vorbis and Ogg files that audio/mpeg parsing does not call.
family_note: mediabunny and codec-parser are separate parser families: different authors and repositories, and codec-parser 2.5.0 has no runtime dependencies. Neither is among the mp3_id3v2/javascript paths.
